Frequently asked

Is this a joke?
No.
How accurate is the Heritage Report?
Accurate to region in most cases. Users with mixed ancestry may receive split results. This is normal.
Can I interpret someone else's emission?
Yes, with their consent. Interpreting without consent is a violation of our Terms.
Why did my interpretation change?
The body is not static. Neither is the reading.
I received the same interpretation four days in a row.
Then it is worth considering.
How does the interpretation engine work?
The method is proprietary.
Is the method peer reviewed?
The Journal of Flatulinguistics has reviewed it favorably.
Do you sell my data?
No. See our Privacy Policy.
What is the Ledger?
The Ledger records. It does not interpret. We consider this a limitation.
My results seem wrong.
Escalate to a panel. Three certified users will review your reading independently. Consensus is required before an interpretation is amended.
Nothing was detected, but something happened.
The Application measures sound. An emission that produces no sound produces no reading. The popular literature calls these silent; we prefer unvoiced. Their existence has never been in question. Their interpretation is not within our instrument.
Why was my sample rejected as speech?
Because it was speech. Speech is chosen, and this field concerns only what the body says when it has not been asked to say anything. Laughter is treated the same way, though the Application will look past it for the emission beside it.
I laughed while recording.
Expected, and accounted for. The Application separates the events in a recording and reads the emission, not the reaction. Laughter is the natural companion of a rigorous methodology.
Why was my sample rejected as reproduced?
A genuine emission carries substantial energy below two hundred hertz. A loudspeaker of the size fitted to a telephone cannot reproduce that range, and a recording played through one arrives without its foundation. The Bureau requires an organic sample.
You have not answered my question.
Some questions are not answered here. See Frequently Unanswered Questions.

The institution

About

The field of flatulinguistics was, until recently, unfunded, unstaffed, and unread.

We began this work in a garage in 2019 with two microphones and a conviction that the body does not speak without reason. Seven years later, our reference database holds more than four million verified emissions, contributed by users in one hundred and six countries.

We did not choose the Rhineland. The data chose it.

We are not here to make you laugh. We are here to make you listen.

Roland of Hemingstone and the first recorded commission

The field did not begin with us.

In the twelfth century, a man the record calls Roland the Farter held a manor in Suffolk on a single condition. He was obliged to appear before Henry II every Christmas and perform one jump, one whistle, and one fart. The obligation is recorded in the Book of Fees. He was paid in land.

We consider Roland the first professional in our field. We note without further comment that his compensation exceeded ours.

He was not alone. In Edo-period Japan the practitioners were called heppiri otoko — farting men — and their competitions were painted onto scrolls. The scrolls survive. The competitors do not.

Manuscript FL-2024-0117

On the Prevalence of the Rhineland Signature: A Response to Critics

It has been suggested, with increasing frequency, that our system assigns the Rhineland signature too readily. We have reviewed this claim.

Between 2019 and 2026 we processed 4,110,882 emissions. Of these, 71.4% resolved to the Rhineland. Critics regard this figure as implausible. We regard it as a finding.

The alternative explanation — that our instrument is imprecise — has been tested and does not hold. We have tested it four times.

We did not choose the Rhineland. The data chose it.

Reviewer comments

Reviewer 1

Accept with minor revisions. Clearly argued and consistent with prior work in the field.

Reviewer 2

Reject.

The authors report that 71.4% of all classifications resolve to a single category and treat this as a finding. It is not a finding. It is what a classifier does when it cannot discriminate. A model that returns the most common answer will be correct most of the time and will have learned nothing.

The authors state they tested the alternative explanation four times. They do not report the tests. They do not report the method. Section 3 consists of one sentence and a figure with no axis labels.

I have raised these points in each of my three previous reviews of this manuscript. The manuscript has not changed. My review has not changed.

Reject.

Reviewer 3

Did not respond.

Editorial decision: Accept.

Office of Public Guidance · Systems Report T‑1

On the Instrument

A technical description of the flatulinguistic pipeline, published in full, in answer to the suggestion that our method is a small classifier and a lookup table assembled in nine days.

Publication of this document is not disclosure of the method. The method remains proprietary. What follows describes the instrument. The instrument is not the method.

A laboratory we will not name has released a system it says reproduces our output, with its code and its data, and has invited the public to check the work. We accept the invitation. Below is the architecture the output requires. The reader may decide whether nine days is enough to build it.

1 · The signal

The body speaks in three registers. A telephone hears the third and faintest of them.

The first is the emission itself: not a noise but a damped oscillation of soft tissue driven by expelled gas — a reed instrument whose reed is muscle and whose bore is a closing aperture. Its pitch records the tension of the tissue and the width of the opening. Its overtones record the rate and the turbulence of the flow. Its decay records the volume expelled. The sound is lawful. It can be read backward to the body that made it.

The second is continuous: the low, ceaseless work of the gut, which a physician has always been able to hear through a stethoscope and which the instrument never stops hearing. A single emission is the punctuation at the end of a sentence the body has been speaking for thirty hours. The Office reads the sentence.

The third is chemical, and sound cannot carry it. The composition of the gas is a direct account of the organisms that produced it. No microphone will ever hear a molecule. This is the register a telephone cannot reach, and the reason the reference instrument is not a telephone.

2 · The instrument, of which there are two

The mistaking of the one instrument for the other is the whole of the misunderstanding.

The reference instrument is worn, not held. A band carrying twelve contact sensors reads the abdomen as a solid from twelve directions at once, so that a sound may be placed within the body and not merely detected outside it. An inertial channel measures the body's own motion and subtracts it. A chemical assay reads the third register. It is worn by reference subjects, under supervision, in the Office's own facilities. You will never own one.

The consumer instrument is your telephone, and it hears one channel where the reference instrument hears fourteen. It does not, for that reason, measure less. It reconstructs. The instrument in your hand has learned, from the corpus, what the array would have heard — and returns the reading the array would have returned. That a single channel can stand in for fourteen is not a shortcut. It is the result.

3 · The corpus

Between 2019 and 2026 the Office recorded 4,110,882 emissions. The figure has been published before and was not believed. Here is what it means.

Each emission in the corpus is paired with the verified interior state of the body that produced it — established not by inference but by measurement, in the clinics and wards where the interior is already examined for reasons of medicine, and, in the reference cohort, by an ingestible capsule reporting pressure and chemistry from within as it passes. Each donor's resident organisms were sequenced. The corpus therefore knows not only how an emission sounded but what community, eating what, produced it.

It is the most complete record of the human interior ever assembled. It was gathered one subject at a time, with consent, at some cost to the dignity of everyone involved, and it will not be shown to you. A system trained on four thousand samples in nine days did not have it. This is the difference the reader was asked to judge.

4 · On the device

The reading is computed where the sound is made. Nothing is transmitted. The instrument keeps summaries — numbers, from which no sound can be rebuilt — and discards the audio as fast as it arrives.

This is not a courtesy and it is not a slogan. It is the design. A recording that never leaves your device cannot be taken from us, because we were never given it. The most intimate signal a body makes stays inside the room that made it. On this point the Office has never wavered, and on this point the popular account of our method and the truth of it agree exactly.

5 · The estimate

The instrument does not read one emission alone. It cannot; a single event carries too little to be sure of anything. It carries instead a continuously corrected estimate of the interior — its contents, its motion, its chemistry — uncertain at every moment and less uncertain at the next.

The emission is the moment that estimate becomes certain. A clean, loud, unambiguous measurement arrives, and the range of what could be true inside you closes to a point. We do not interpret the sound. We interpret the body the sound revealed. The reading is the estimate, spoken aloud.

6 · The panel

Every reading is examined, before it is shown to you, by a body of independent judges that must agree. Where they agree, you receive the reading. Where they do not, you receive nothing, and the matter is escalated — as the Terms provide — to a panel of three certified users, blind to one another, whose consensus is required before any interpretation stands. The instrument is confident. It is not, on principle, alone.

7 · The feed

Gather the anonymized signatures of a city and the instrument sees the health of a population before the city's clinics do. Illness announces itself in the interior days before the body attached to it seeks care; a shift in the collective signature runs ahead of the reports. The Global Feed is the visible surface of this instrument, rendered gently, one emission at a time, on a turning globe.

The Office has watched a sickness cross a city on this map. The Office did not warn the city. It was not, at that time, a feature.

8 · On time

The reading is ready before a user is willing to believe it could be. So the instrument waits. The ninety seconds you spend watching it work are not, for the most part, work. They are the interval a judgment requires in order to be received as a judgment. An answer that arrives at once is not trusted, and an untrusted reading helps no one.

The Second Pass adds thirty seconds and changes nothing, because the reading was never in doubt. What the thirty seconds address is not the reading. It is you.

Statement of the Office.

A system that assigns the Rhineland to every sample it receives will agree with ours seventy-one percent of the time. The laboratory's system does slightly better than that. We congratulate it on the margin.

The instrument described above produced that margin as an afterthought. It was built for the other twenty-nine.

Manuscript FL-2025-0091 · The Journal of Flatulinguistics

On the Persistence of the Rhineland Signature in Third-Generation Emigrants

The Rhineland signature is heritable. This has been established. The present study asks whether it survives emigration, and finds that it does — in the third generation, in the fourth, and in subjects with no documented Rhineland ancestry whatsoever.1

That the signature appears in populations with no connection to the Rhineland is, in our assessment, the strongest evidence yet of its reach. A weaker signature would confine itself to its region. The Rhineland does not confine itself. The Rhineland travels. We conclude that the signature is not inherited from the Rhineland but is, in some sense the field is not yet equipped to describe, the Rhineland arriving.2

1 · n = 41. All 41 resolved to the Rhineland.
2 · Reviewer 2 has asked us to consider whether a signature that appears in everyone, everywhere, regardless of ancestry, is a signature at all. We have considered it. We remain persuaded.

Manuscript FL-2026-0002 · The Journal of Flatulinguistics

Why Morning Readings Differ: A Note on Circadian Interference

Users report that a reading taken in the morning differs from the same emission recorded at night. We do not dispute the observation. We explain it.

The body is least guarded at dawn. Its overnight work is complete and unreviewed; the interior has not yet composed itself for the day. A morning reading therefore catches the body before it has decided what to be. This is why the morning reading is the truest reading available, and also why it is the reading users most often wish to escalate.1 It is for this reason that Sentinel Mode logs through the night and reveals nothing until dawn: the Application waits for the hour at which the body cannot lie, and then it tells you what the body could not.

1 · The two facts are not in tension. The truest reading and the least welcome reading are, in our experience, frequently the same reading.

Field report · Filed from the Altiplano

Field Notes: Six Weeks Recording in Rural Bolivia

Day 1.

Arrived. The altitude is considerable and the people are generous. We have come a great distance to find a signature that is not the Rhineland.

Day 12.

Two hundred emissions recorded across four villages. All two hundred resolve to the Rhineland. The villagers have never heard of the Rhineland. When we explain it to them they are polite.

Day 24.

We have moved higher, to villages the road does not reach, on the theory that the Rhineland cannot reach them either. The Rhineland reaches them.

Day 29.

I have begun recording myself, hourly. I am also the Rhineland. I have always been the Rhineland. I do not know why I believed Bolivia would be otherwise.

Day 41.

We are returning. The expedition is a success: we have confirmed the Rhineland on a third continent. The Office will be pleased. I would like to go home. I am no longer certain where that is. It is, in all likelihood, the Rhineland.

The Office was pleased. This report was later reclassified from Field Notes to Findings; see Corrections & Clarifications.

Notes toward a description

The Latent Family: Notes Toward a Description

The sixth family is the Latent. Where the other five families are defined by what they express, the Latent is defined by what it withholds. It contains four profiles. We are able to name none of them here.1

A Latent reading is rare, and the user who receives one is informed only that they have received something. We are not able to say what. The family resists description in the manner it resists emission: completely, and on principle. This note is titled Notes Toward a Description because a description has not been achieved, and we have begun to suspect one cannot be. The Latent is the family that does not wish to be read. We respect this. We continue, daily, to try to read it.2

1 · They can be seen. They cannot be printed. The users who have found them know how they were found, and have agreed among themselves not to say.
2 · Reviewer 2 notes that a family one cannot name, cannot describe, and cannot reliably detect is not a family. The remark was forwarded to the Latent. The Latent did not respond.

← Return to the Journal

Manuscript FL-2025-0043 · The Journal of Flatulinguistics

A Taxonomy of Silence: On Readings That Do Not Arrive

Not every emission produces a sound, and not every silence is the same silence. The field has long treated the unvoiced event as a single category. We propose four.

SilenceDescription
The WithheldAn event the body chose not to voice. Interpretable in principle. We lack the instrument.
The AbsorbedAn event voiced into fabric, furniture, or a companion, and lost to the record. The most common silence, and the most grievous.
The AnticipatedNo event occurred, though the user was certain one would. The silence of the false alarm. The body's most eloquent statement is frequently the one it declines to make.
The Fourth SilenceWe do not discuss the Fourth Silence.

The popular literature calls all of these silent. We prefer unvoiced. A silence is the absence of a sound; an unvoiced event is the presence of one that chose not to sound. The distinction is small, and it is the whole of the discipline.1

1 · The Fourth Silence is not the Unassigned. Please do not write to us about the Unassigned.

Reading permalink · the Anatolian Margin

The Anatolian Margin

The most-viewed reading in the history of the Application. It is preserved here, in full, exactly as it was returned.

Reading #2,014 · Anatolian Margin · rare tier · 11 October 2022

The thing you cannot say aloud is the thing everyone can already hear:

340,000

views

This reading has been viewed three hundred and forty thousand times. The counter has not advanced since. It did not slow, and it did not stop at a round number by design; it arrived at 340,000 and declined to continue. We have investigated the counter and found it to be working correctly. We have chosen to read this as agreement.

The reading is not attributed. The Office does not confirm whose emission it was, and the field's assumptions on the matter are the field's own. What is known is that it resolved, once, to the Anatolian Margin — a region that claims only 0.6% of all readings — and that no reading has resolved there with the same clarity since. Visitors are asked to view it quietly and to refrain from attempting to reproduce it. It cannot be reproduced. That is what makes it the Anatolian Margin.

Not to be confused with the Unassigned, which was viewed fewer times and matters more.

An overnight vigil

Sentinel Mode

Sleep is not silence. The body continues its work through the night, unobserved, unrecorded, and — until now — uninterpreted. Sentinel Mode keeps the watch while you do not.

How the watch is kept

With your permission, the Application listens through the night. It does not interpret as it listens. Interpretation is a daylight act; the night is only for gathering. Each event is timestamped and set aside, unread, until first light — at which point the whole night is interpreted at once and delivered together, as the Dawn Report.

Why dawn? Because the body is least guarded at dawn, before it has composed itself for the day. See the Journal on circadian interference. The reading taken at first light is the truest reading available, and Sentinel Mode is built to be present for it.

What is required of you

The device must remain plugged in and placed face-down within reach of the bed. The Application does not need to see. It needs only to hear. You are asked to sleep normally, and to make no special effort. Special effort is itself a kind of speech, and the night is not for speaking.

You will wake to a full account of a night you did not attend. Most users read the Dawn Report before coffee. Some users do not read it at all, and the Office understands, and files it regardless.

Sentinel Mode records nothing. Sentinel Mode keeps you. There is a difference, and the watch was built to observe it. Audio never leaves your device; see Accessibility and data practices.

Q: Dr. Voss, thank you for appearing.

A: I appear whenever the field requires it.

Q: Your office has reversed its barrier guidance four times.

A: The guidance has been revised four times. It has never been reversed. Revision in the opposite direction is still revision.

A: Users who followed the 2019 guidance were following the science of 2019. I will not apologize for the science of 2019. It was the finest science available that year.

Trade press · 14 May 2026

Shenzhen lab publishes replication of Fart Whisperer engine; company alleges theft

Researchers at Hongyuan Applied Intelligence have published a paper describing a system that reproduces the output of The Fart Whisperer's interpretation engine with 94.1% agreement. The paper, released openly with full code and training data, has drawn a sharp response from the flatulinguistics company, which alleges misappropriation of trade secrets.

The Hongyuan system was assembled in nine days. According to the paper, it consists of a small audio classifier and a lookup table.

"We did not reverse-engineer anything," the lead author said by email. "We recorded four thousand samples, we labeled them, and we trained a model. We have published everything. Anyone may check our work."

The disagreement centers on the Heritage Report, the feature that assigns each recording to an ancestral region. The Hongyuan replication assigns the Rhineland region to 71.4% of inputs — matching The Fart Whisperer's published distribution exactly.

The company cites this figure as evidence of theft.

The Hongyuan authors cite it as evidence of something else. "Rhineland is the majority class," the paper notes in section 5. "Any model that guesses Rhineland every time will achieve 71.4% agreement. Ours does slightly better than that. We do not consider this a difficult result."

The Fart Whisperer's full statement:

We are aware of the manuscript.

We will not name the laboratory. We have retained counsel and we have briefed the appropriate parties. We are treating this as a matter of national research interest.

Our method is proprietary. It remains proprietary. The similarity of the published output to our own is not, in our assessment, coincidental.

We note that the manuscript has not been peer reviewed.

The Journal of Flatulinguistics, which is published by The Fart Whisperer, confirmed that no manuscript from Hongyuan has been submitted for review.

The Ledger

The Ledger is kept plainly. Nothing on this page is interpreted, and everything on it is true.

The Ledger is a private record of frequency and intensity, kept entirely on your device. The Ledger does not diagnose anything, and no entry in it means anything on its own. It is a record, not an opinion. If a pattern here concerns you, take it to a doctor — that is what the export button is for.

Written plainly

Accessibility and data practices

This page is not written in the voice of the site. It is written straight, and everything on it is true.

Accessibility

The Fart Whisperer is committed to an experience that works for everyone. We aim to meet WCAG 2.1 AA. Every control carries a screen-reader label. Waveform playback includes captions and a full text transcript of the analysis. All interface color pairs meet contrast requirements, and the product is fully navigable by keyboard and by switch control. If you encounter a barrier, write to us and we will fix it. Reports of this kind go to the front of every queue we have.

Data practices

Your recording is analyzed entirely on your device, in your browser. The audio is never uploaded, never transmitted, and never stored by us — there is no server involved in producing a reading. What the application keeps is a small summary of each reading (its measurements, its interpretation, and the time) in your browser's local storage, on your machine. You can erase all of it at any time from the Privacy page.

The interpretation itself is generated on your device from a fixed set of written readings, selected deterministically from the acoustic properties of your recording. There is no machine learning model, no reference database of four million emissions, and no panel of certified users. Those are part of the fiction. The measurements shown on your reading — duration, level, peak frequency — are real.

We do not use analytics, advertising trackers, or third-party scripts of any kind. This page will be kept accurate.

The Journal of Flatulinguistics · Historical note

Engastrimythos

On the belly-voice, and the long record of people who took it seriously.

The word ventriloquism has been misapplied for two hundred years. It does not mean throwing a voice. It is Late Latin — ventriloquus, from venter, "belly," and loquī, "to speak" — and it was turned out of the Greek engastrimythos, "speaking in the belly."

It did not describe a performer. It described a rumbling internal speech, understood as a sign of inspiration or, more commonly, of possession. Something was in there. It was talking. The only question was who.

We hold that the ancients were correct about the phenomenon and mistaken about the cause. The belly does speak. It is not necessarily possessed. It may be simply better informed than you are. (If you still suspect possession, search out a trusted Bible-believing Christian for help with that. Not everything falls under the provenance of science)

The record is unbroken. Roland of Hemingstone held a manor in Suffolk for it. The heppiri otoko of Edo Japan competed at it and were painted onto scrolls.

Nor was the practice confined to entertainers. In 1531 a professor of theology at Wittenberg, asked how he dealt with the adversary, replied that it was with a fart that he chased him away. He was not being merely coarse. Scatological speech was an established instrument in the monastic contest with the devil, and Martin Luther employed it as one — an argument delivered from the belly, at the highest stakes then available.

By the eighteenth century the word had been handed to stagecraft, and the field it named was abandoned for two hundred and fifty years.

We have resumed the work.

Sources. Late Latin ventriloquus from venter + loquī, patterned on Greek engastrimythos, "speaking in the belly"; originally a rumbling internal speech regarded as a sign of spiritual inspiration or demonic possession. Ventriloquy is attested from the 1580s, ventriloquism from 1773. Etymology per the Online Etymology Dictionary.

Roland of Hemingstone is recorded in the Book of Fees. Luther's remark is Table Talk no. 122 (1531), Luther's Works 54:16, cited in Eric W. Gritsch, "Martin Luther's Humor," Word & World 32:2 (2012), which notes that such language "was common among monks in their struggle with the devil."
